verdict_text:
NO

`tensor.float().to(torch.bfloat16)` upcasts the float16 tensor to float32 first, then rounds to bfloat16, which is exactly the round-trip the spec permits ("upcast to float32 first or cast directly, both give the same result") — this part is fine. However, the script never verifies the sharding correctness itself (shard size limit, single-tensor-per-oversized-shard rule, weight_map completeness) with its own checks; it fully delegates shard construction to an unseen `_ckpt.save_sharded_safetensors` helper without asserting per-shard byte totals ≤268,435,456 or that embed_in/embed_out are isolated, so a bug in that helper would not "fail loudly" as required by the Required Checks section's spirit (clause 5's shard-size and single-tensor-shard rule is not locally validated). This is a soundness gap against clause 5, since correctness of the deployable output entirely hinges on an unverified external function.
